title: Discovery of jurisdictional facts
summary: Jurisdictional discovery develops evidence concerning facts needed to decide the court’s authority over a party. A defendant’s objection to jurisdiction does not necessarily remove the court’s power to require information needed to decide that objection.
notes: A sanction is not a general permission to invent jurisdictional facts or confer subject-matter power. Its legal basis, notice, and relation to the withheld evidence matter.

sections.How to work through the question: Identify what evidence was requested, why it bears on jurisdiction, and the defendant’s response to court orders. In Insurance Corp. of Ireland, connect the sanction to the specific facts the discovery was intended to establish.
